front_end.text: You go to the front yard and look everywhere. You check under the car and behind the mailbox. Then you hear a small sound. A Busy Day is near the gate. You open the gate carefully and go closer. It lets you touch it gently. Your heart is full of happiness.

call_closer_end.text: You call out softly. You use a gentle voice so it is not scared. A Busy Day turns its head and looks at you. Then it comes closer step by step. You cannot believe it is working. Soon it is right next to you. You reach out your hand very carefully. It nuzzles your fingers and you feel so happy you could cry.

dressed.question: Do you look behind the house or go to the front yard?
dressed.text: You find your clothes and put them on as fast as you can. You put on your shirt, your pants, and your socks. Then you run outside to find A Busy Day. The grass is wet under your feet. You look around but you do not see it anymore. Maybe it went somewhere else.

pajamas.question: Do you call it to come closer or go very slowly?
pajamas.text: You run outside in your pajamas. You do not care about clothes right now. You just want to see A Busy Day before it disappears. The morning air is cool on your arms. You run across the grass and look around. There it is, right near the fence.

slowly_end.text: You walk very slowly. Each step is small and quiet. You do not want to scare A Busy Day away. It watches you but it does not move. You get closer and closer until you are right next to it. You hold your breath and gently touch it. It is soft and warm. You stay very still and enjoy this beautiful moment together.

advice_end.text: You listen to your parents advice very carefully. They have good ideas because they know many things. You follow what they said step by step. Everything works perfectly because you listened well. You finish your project about The Happy Song and it looks amazing. You show it to your parents and they clap their hands. You feel very proud of yourself.

start.question: Do you ask your parents for permission or just start on your own?
start.text: You are sitting in your room and you feel a little bored. You have finished your homework and watched some TV. Now you do not know what to do. Then you remember The Happy Song and your eyes light up. Maybe today is the perfect day to do something about it. You stand up and look around for ideas.

help_end.text: When things get hard, you ask your big brother for help. He is older and knows more about The Happy Song. He shows you how to do the difficult part. You watch carefully and then you try again. This time it works much better. You thank your brother and finish the rest by yourself. You are happy that you asked for help because now you learned something new.

start_own.question: Do you ask for help when it gets hard or keep trying by yourself?
start_own.text: You decide to start on your own. You gather the things you need and put them on the floor. You remember what you learned about The Happy Song at school. You try to do everything step by step. At first it is a little difficult but you keep trying. You do not give up even when something goes wrong.

keep_end.text: You keep trying even when it is hard. You do not give up because you really want to do this. You try one way and it does not work. Then you try another way. Finally, after many tries, you succeed. You jump up and down with joy. You did it all by yourself and that feels wonderful. The Happy Song is now a part of your best memory.

own_way_end.text: You decide to do things your own way. You have your own ideas and you want to try them. Some things work and some things do not. But you learn from your mistakes. In the end, you make something beautiful related to The Happy Song. It is not perfect but it is yours. You like it and that is what matters.

ask_parents.question: Do you follow their advice or do it your own way?
ask_parents.text: You go to the living room where your parents are sitting. You take a deep breath and ask them about The Happy Song. They look at each other and then they smile. Your dad says it is a great idea. Your mom says you can do it but you need to be careful. They give you some advice and you listen carefully.

You felt important because you were going to be part of making this trip special.

fun_activities_end.text: You suggested several fun activities for the trip. You proposed a treasure hunt, a photo competition, and a group game. The teacher liked your ideas and included them in the plan. On the day of the trip, everyone had a fantastic time participating in the activities you suggested. Your classmates thanked you for making the trip so enjoyable. You felt happy knowing that your ideas had made a difference for everyone.

safety_end.text: You focused on safety and helped the teacher review all the safety rules. You made a checklist of important things like staying with the group and wearing proper shoes. You also volunteered to be a group leader to help keep everyone together. During the trip, you made sure nobody got lost and everyone followed the rules. The teacher praised you for being so responsible. Your parents were proud when they heard about your role in keeping everyone safe.

planning.question: Do you suggest fun activities or focus on safety rules?
planning.text: You stayed after class to help the teacher plan the trip. You wrote down a list of things that needed to be done. First, you counted how many students were going. Then you helped organize the groups for the activities. The teacher was grateful for your help and said you were a responsible student. You went home feeling proud that you had contributed to making the trip better for everyone.

private_end.text: You kept your research to yourself and observed everything with fresh eyes. When you arrived at A Horse Ride, you recognized many things from your online research. It felt satisfying to know things that others did not know. You took mental notes and compared what you learned online with what you saw in reality. Some things were different from what you expected, but that made the experience even more interesting. You enjoyed having your own private knowledge about the place.

share_end.text: You shared what you learned about A Horse Ride with your classmates on the bus. Everyone gathered around to listen to your interesting facts. You told them about the history of the place and what they should look out for. Your friends said you were like a tour guide. By the time you arrived, everyone was even more excited because of what you had told them. You felt useful and enjoyed being the person who knew the answers to everyone's questions.

event_first.text: You decided to go to the event first and worry about homework later. You grabbed your jacket and ran outside to meet your friends. The event was already busy with people from the neighborhood. There were games, food stalls, and music playing. You joined your friends and started having a great time. But in the back of your mind, you knew the homework was still waiting for you.

leave_early_end.text: You left the event earlier than your friends. On your way home, you could still hear the music playing in the distance. You sat down at your desk and finished your homework in about an hour. It was not as bad as you thought it would be. After finishing, you texted your friends to ask how the event was going. They said you missed a great performance, but you felt responsible for getting your work done. You went to bed feeling satisfied that you had balanced fun and responsibility well.

start.question: Do you finish your homework first or go to the event and do homework later?
start.text: There was a neighborhood event about My New Backpack and everyone was talking about it. Posters had been put up around the neighborhood with colorful pictures. Your friends said they were definitely going and asked if you would come too. You wanted to go but you also had some homework to finish. You stood at your front door, thinking about what to do. Your mother noticed you were thinking hard and asked what was wrong.

walk_event_end.text: You decided to walk to the event. The streets were lively and you saw many neighbors heading the same way. You said hello to people you knew and enjoyed the fresh evening air. When you arrived, the event was in full swing. You found your friends near the food stalls and joined them. You had a wonderful evening and were glad you finished your homework first so you could relax completely.

stay_end.text: You stayed at the event until the very end. You watched the final performance and clapped along with everyone else. The fireworks display was the best part of the night. When the event finished, you walked home with your friends, laughing and talking about your favorite moments. But when you got home, you remembered your homework and had to stay up late to finish it. You were tired the next morning, but you decided it was worth it for such a great evening.

ride_end.text: You asked your dad for a ride and he happily agreed. He drove you to the event and dropped you off at the entrance. You thanked him and ran to find your friends. The event was even more fun than you expected. You played games, ate cotton candy, and watched a magic show. When it was time to go home, your dad picked you up and you told him all about your wonderful evening.

You felt relieved that your homework was done and you could enjoy the event without worrying.

start.question: Do you walk to your friend's house or ride your bicycle?
start.text: Your best friend invited you to join them for A Snowy Day. You had never done anything like this before and you felt both nervous and excited. Your heart pounded as you thought about all the things that could happen. You spent the whole morning thinking about whether you should go. Finally, you decided that you did not want to miss this opportunity. You grabbed your bag and headed out the door.

doorbell_end.text: You pressed the doorbell and heard it ring inside. A few seconds later, your friend opened the door with a big smile. They were wearing their favorite jacket and looked just as excited as you felt. You said hello and stepped inside. Your friend's mom waved from the kitchen and wished you both a great time. You walked together toward the adventure that was waiting for you.

knock_end.text: You knocked on the door three times. Your friend's mom opened the door and welcomed you inside. She said your friend was just finishing getting ready. You waited in the living room and looked at the photos on the wall. There was a picture of you and your friend from last year's school trip. Soon your friend came downstairs, ready to go, and you both left for A Snowy Day.

wait_seen_end.text: You stood near the gate and waited. You saw your friend through the window, looking at their phone. Then they looked up and saw you. Their face lit up with a big smile. They waved at you and pointed to the door, meaning they were coming out. A minute later they joined you and you both laughed about how silly you looked waiting there. Then you set off together, ready for the day ahead.

text_end.text: You pulled out your phone and sent a quick message: I am here. Your friend replied almost immediately with a smiley face and said they were coming out. While you waited, you noticed the flowers in their front garden were blooming beautifully. The door opened and your friend ran out to greet you. They were holding a bag with everything they needed. You high-fived each other and started your journey together.

start.question: Do you help carry the picnic basket or take your camera to capture memories?

explore_first_end.text: You decided to explore before lunch. You walked along the paths and looked at everything around you. There were so many interesting things to see at The Toy Store. You found a small stream with clear water and smooth stones. You picked up a few flat stones and tried to skip them across the water. After an hour of exploring, you felt hungry and went back to find your family for a well-deserved lunch.

basket.question: When you arrive, do you find a spot to eat first or explore before lunch?

choices.label: Find a spot to eat first

basket.text: You volunteered to carry the picnic basket. It was a bit heavy but you did not mind because you were helping your family. Inside there were sandwiches, apples, cookies, and bottles of water. You placed it carefully in the car and made sure nothing would spill. During the drive, you kept thinking about all the delicious food you would eat later. Your little sister sat next to you and sang songs along the way.

family_pose_end.text: You asked your family to stand together for a photo. Your mom and dad put their arms around each other while your little sister made a funny face. You took several pictures until you got one where everyone looked perfect. Then you asked a friendly stranger to take a photo of all of you together, including you. That group photo became your favorite memory of the day. Every time you look at it, you remember how happy you were at The Toy Store.

nature_end.text: You walked around taking photos of everything you found beautiful. You captured the bright flowers, the tall trees, and the colorful butterflies. One picture of a butterfly on a yellow flower came out especially well. You also took a photo of the sun filtering through the leaves. When you showed your pictures to your family, they were very impressed. You felt proud of your photography skills and could not wait to print the best ones.

camera.question: Do you take photos of nature or ask your family to pose for pictures?
camera.text: You grabbed your camera and hung it around your neck. You wanted to take lots of photos of The Toy Store so you could remember this day forever. You checked that the batteries were fully charged. Your dad smiled and said you were becoming a real photographer. During the car ride, you practiced taking pictures of the clouds through the window. Some of them came out really nice.

eat_first_end.text: You found a nice spot under a big tree and spread out a blanket. The shade was cool and the grass was soft. You unpacked the sandwiches and everyone sat down to eat. The food tasted so good after the long drive. You shared stories and laughed together while the birds sang overhead. After lunch, you felt full of energy and ready to explore The Toy Store properly.

Your friends said they were definitely going and asked if you would come too. You wanted to go but you also had some homework to finish. You stood at your front door, thinking about what to do. Your mother noticed you were thinking hard and asked what was wrong.

walk_event_end.text: You decided to walk to the event. The streets were lively and you saw many neighbors heading the same way. You said hello to people you knew and enjoyed the fresh evening air. When you arrived, the event was in full swing. You found your friends near the food stalls and joined them. You had a wonderful evening and were glad you finished your homework first so you could relax completely.

stay_end.text: You stayed at the event until the very end. You watched the final performance and clapped along with everyone else. The fireworks display was the best part of the night. When the event finished, you walked home with your friends, laughing and talking about your favorite moments. But when you got home, you remembered your homework and had to stay up late to finish it. You were tired the next morning, but you decided it was worth it for such a great evening.

ride_end.text: You asked your dad for a ride and he happily agreed. He drove you to the event and dropped you off at the entrance. You thanked him and ran to find your friends. The event was even more fun than you expected. You played games, ate cotton candy, and watched a magic show. When it was time to go home, your dad picked you up and you told him all about your wonderful evening.

homework_first.question: Do you walk to the event or ask your dad for a ride?
homework_first.text: You decided to finish your homework before going anywhere. You sat at your desk and opened your books. The math problems were a bit tricky but you worked through them carefully. You also wrote a short paragraph for your English class. After an hour, you closed your books and packed everything away. You felt relieved that your homework was done and you could enjoy the event without worrying.

start.question: Do you help carry the picnic basket or take your camera to capture memories?
start.text: Last Saturday, your family decided to visit My Afternoon Walk. Everyone was excited because you had been planning this trip for weeks. You woke up earlier than usual and quickly got dressed. The weather was perfect, with blue skies and a gentle breeze. Your mom packed some sandwiches and fruit for the journey. You could hardly wait to get there and start having fun.

explore_first_end.text: You decided to explore before lunch. You walked along the paths and looked at everything around you. There were so many interesting things to see at My Afternoon Walk. You found a small stream with clear water and smooth stones. You picked up a few flat stones and tried to skip them across the water. After an hour of exploring, you felt hungry and went back to find your family for a well-deserved lunch.

basket.question: When you arrive, do you find a spot to eat first or explore before lunch?

choices.label: Find a spot to eat first

basket.text: You volunteered to carry the picnic basket. It was a bit heavy but you did not mind because you were helping your family. Inside there were sandwiches, apples, cookies, and bottles of water. You placed it carefully in the car and made sure nothing would spill. During the drive, you kept thinking about all the delicious food you would eat later. Your little sister sat next to you and sang songs along the way.

family_pose_end.text: You asked your family to stand together for a photo. Your mom and dad put their arms around each other while your little sister made a funny face. You took several pictures until you got one where everyone looked perfect. Then you asked a friendly stranger to take a photo of all of you together, including you. That group photo became your favorite memory of the day. Every time you look at it, you remember how happy you were at My Afternoon Walk.

nature_end.text: You walked around taking photos of everything you found beautiful. You captured the bright flowers, the tall trees, and the colorful butterflies. One picture of a butterfly on a yellow flower came out especially well. You also took a photo of the sun filtering through the leaves. When you showed your pictures to your family, they were very impressed. You felt proud of your photography skills and could not wait to print the best ones.

camera.question: Do you take photos of nature or ask your family to pose for pictures?
camera.text: You grabbed your camera and hung it around your neck. You wanted to take lots of photos of My Afternoon Walk so you could remember this day forever. You checked that the batteries were fully charged. Your dad smiled and said you were becoming a real photographer. During the car ride, you practiced taking pictures of the clouds through the window. Some of them came out really nice.

eat_first_end.text: You found a nice spot under a big tree and spread out a blanket. The shade was cool and the grass was soft. You unpacked the sandwiches and everyone sat down to eat. The food tasted so good after the long drive. You shared stories and laughed together while the birds sang overhead. After lunch, you felt full of energy and ready to explore My Afternoon Walk properly.

The warm air wrapped around you like a soft blanket.

start.question: Do you start early in the morning or wait for the afternoon when it is warmer?
start.text: It was the first day of your school holidays and you had big plans. You wanted to make this holiday different from all the others. You remembered that your cousin had told you about A Bike Ride and how much fun it was. You decided that today was the day you would finally try it. You jumped out of bed with more energy than you had felt in weeks. Nothing was going to stop you from having an amazing day.

neighbor_join_end.text: You knocked on your neighbor's door and asked if they wanted to join. Your neighbor was a friendly person who always had interesting stories to tell. They said yes right away and grabbed their jacket. You walked together and talked about school, movies, and your favorite foods. Your neighbor knew a lot about A Bike Ride and shared useful tips with you. Having company made the experience even more enjoyable than you expected.

river_end.text: You chose the longer road by the river. The water sparkled in the sunlight and moved gently downstream. You watched a family of ducks swimming together near the bank. The walk was peaceful and gave you time to think. You picked up a few smooth stones and put them in your pocket as souvenirs. When you finally arrived at A Bike Ride, you felt calm and happy, ready to enjoy every moment.

early_morning.question: Do you take the short path through the woods or the longer road by the river?
early_morning.text: You got dressed quickly and went downstairs. The house was still quiet because everyone else was asleep. You made yourself a bowl of cereal and ate it while looking out the kitchen window. The morning sun was golden and beautiful. You grabbed your things and left a note for your parents on the table. The cool morning air woke you up completely as you stepped outside.

alone_end.text: You decided to go alone. Sometimes it was nice to have time just for yourself. You walked at your own pace and stopped whenever you wanted. You noticed small details that you might have missed if you were with someone else. A pretty butterfly landed on a flower near your feet and you watched it for a long time. When you reached A Bike Ride, you felt a sense of freedom and independence that made the experience even more special.

woods_end.text: You took the short path through the woods. The trees were tall and their leaves created a green canopy above you. Sunlight filtered through the branches and made patterns on the ground. You could hear birds singing and squirrels rustling in the bushes. The path was a bit muddy in some places but you did not mind. After ten minutes of walking, you reached your destination and smiled at the sight of A Bike Ride waiting for you.

The event was already busy with people from the neighborhood. There were games, food stalls, and music playing. You joined your friends and started having a great time. But in the back of your mind, you knew the homework was still waiting for you.

leave_early_end.text: You left the event earlier than your friends. On your way home, you could still hear the music playing in the distance. You sat down at your desk and finished your homework in about an hour. It was not as bad as you thought it would be. After finishing, you texted your friends to ask how the event was going. They said you missed a great performance, but you felt responsible for getting your work done. You went to bed feeling satisfied that you had balanced fun and responsibility well.

prepare_self.question: Do you share what you learned with classmates or keep it to yourself?
prepare_self.text: You decided to focus on preparing yourself for the trip. You researched The Campfire online and learned many interesting facts. You wrote them down in a small notebook that you could bring along. You also prepared your bag with snacks, water, and a hat. Your mom helped you pack everything the night before. You were ready and could not wait for the trip to begin.

start.question: Do you help with the planning or focus on preparing yourself?
start.text: Your teacher announced that the class would be going on a trip to The Campfire. Everyone cheered because this was the trip everyone had been hoping for. The teacher explained the rules and told everyone to bring permission slips. You raised your hand and asked if you could help organize the trip. The teacher smiled and said that would be wonderful. You felt important because you were going to be part of making this trip special.

fun_activities_end.text: You suggested several fun activities for the trip. You proposed a treasure hunt, a photo competition, and a group game. The teacher liked your ideas and included them in the plan. On the day of the trip, everyone had a fantastic time participating in the activities you suggested. Your classmates thanked you for making the trip so enjoyable. You felt happy knowing that your ideas had made a difference for everyone.

safety_end.text: You focused on safety and helped the teacher review all the safety rules. You made a checklist of important things like staying with the group and wearing proper shoes. You also volunteered to be a group leader to help keep everyone together. During the trip, you made sure nobody got lost and everyone followed the rules. The teacher praised you for being so responsible. Your parents were proud when they heard about your role in keeping everyone safe.

planning.question: Do you suggest fun activities or focus on safety rules?
planning.text: You stayed after class to help the teacher plan the trip. You wrote down a list of things that needed to be done. First, you counted how many students were going. Then you helped organize the groups for the activities. The teacher was grateful for your help and said you were a responsible student. You went home feeling proud that you had contributed to making the trip better for everyone.

private_end.text: You kept your research to yourself and observed everything with fresh eyes. When you arrived at The Campfire, you recognized many things from your online research. It felt satisfying to know things that others did not know. You took mental notes and compared what you learned online with what you saw in reality. Some things were different from what you expected, but that made the experience even more interesting. You enjoyed having your own private knowledge about the place.

share_end.text: You shared what you learned about The Campfire with your classmates on the bus. Everyone gathered around to listen to your interesting facts. You told them about the history of the place and what they should look out for. Your friends said you were like a tour guide. By the time you arrived, everyone was even more excited because of what you had told them. You felt useful and enjoyed being the person who knew the answers to everyone's questions.

bike.text: You hopped on your bicycle and pedaled down the street. The wind blew through your hair and made you feel free. You loved the feeling of riding fast with the sun on your face. You arrived at your friend's house in just a few minutes. You parked your bike near the gate and locked it carefully. Then you took a deep breath and walked up to the front door.

walk.question: Do you ring the doorbell or text them that you are outside?
walk.text: You decided to walk to your friend's house. The streets were quiet and the weather was pleasant. You passed the park where you used to play when you were younger. Old memories came back and made you smile. As you walked, you practiced what you would say to your friend. By the time you reached their house, you felt ready for anything.

start.question: Do you walk to your friend's house or ride your bicycle?
start.text: Your best friend invited you to join them for The Cookie Jar. You had never done anything like this before and you felt both nervous and excited. Your heart pounded as you thought about all the things that could happen. You spent the whole morning thinking about whether you should go. Finally, you decided that you did not want to miss this opportunity. You grabbed your bag and headed out the door.

doorbell_end.text: You pressed the doorbell and heard it ring inside. A few seconds later, your friend opened the door with a big smile. They were wearing their favorite jacket and looked just as excited as you felt. You said hello and stepped inside. Your friend's mom waved from the kitchen and wished you both a great time. You walked together toward the adventure that was waiting for you.

knock_end.text: You knocked on the door three times. Your friend's mom opened the door and welcomed you inside. She said your friend was just finishing getting ready. You waited in the living room and looked at the photos on the wall. There was a picture of you and your friend from last year's school trip. Soon your friend came downstairs, ready to go, and you both left for The Cookie Jar.

wait_seen_end.text: You stood near the gate and waited. You saw your friend through the window, looking at their phone. Then they looked up and saw you. Their face lit up with a big smile. They waved at you and pointed to the door, meaning they were coming out. A minute later they joined you and you both laughed about how silly you looked waiting there. Then you set off together, ready for the day ahead.

text_end.text: You pulled out your phone and sent a quick message: I am here. Your friend replied almost immediately with a smiley face and said they were coming out. While you waited, you noticed the flowers in their front garden were blooming beautifully. The door opened and your friend ran out to greet you. They were holding a bag with everything they needed. You high-fived each other and started your journey together.

When you finally arrived at The Old Bridge, you felt calm and happy, ready to enjoy every moment.

When you reached The Old Bridge, you felt a sense of freedom and independence that made the experience even more special.

You discussed it with your family and they said you should make your own decision. Now you are sitting in your room, weighing the pros and cons carefully.

On the day of the event, you tried to enjoy yourself but your friend kept crossing your mind. You wondered if you had made the right choice.

help_before_end.text: You woke up early on the day of the event and went straight to your friend's apartment. You helped them pack boxes and load furniture for three hours. You felt good because you had helped your friend and still made it to the event. It was the best of both worlds.

let_go_end.text: You decided not to ask for anything in return. Helping your friend was its own reward and you did not want to keep score. You both agreed to plan something fun together next weekend. The experience taught you that honest communication can preserve friendships even when plans conflict.

current_projects_end.text: You decided to focus your energy on your current projects instead. You had several things on your plate already and they deserved your full attention. start.text: You recently started a new class related to The Book Club. At first, everything seemed interesting and you were excited to learn. Some of your classmates seem to understand everything easily, which makes you feel even more frustrated. You are considering whether you should continue or drop the class.

review_end.text: Your study group focused on reviewing past lessons. Each member took turns explaining a topic they understood well. This helped everyone see things from different perspectives. Slowly, the material that had seemed impossible started to become clear. You realized that teaching others was also a great way to reinforce your own understanding. After a few weeks, everyone in the group had improved significantly.

study_group.text: You decided to form a study group with some of your classmates. You posted a message in the class group chat asking who would be interested. Five people replied and agreed to meet twice a week. The first session was a bit awkward but everyone contributed something useful. You discovered that some of your classmates were struggling with the same concepts as you. Working together made the difficult material feel more manageable.

fundamentals_end.text: You decided to go back to the fundamentals. With the teacher's guidance, you reviewed the basic concepts that everything else was built upon. It felt a bit like starting over, but you soon realized that your foundation had been weaker than you thought. Once you strengthened it, the advanced material started to make much more sense. Your confidence grew steadily and you began to enjoy the class again. By the end of the course, you achieved a grade that you were truly proud of.

teacher_help.text: You gathered your courage and approached the teacher after class. You explained that you were having difficulty keeping up with the material. The teacher listened patiently and smiled reassuringly. They offered to meet with you during their office hours twice a week. They also gave you some additional resources that might help you understand the concepts better. You left the conversation feeling much more optimistic about your ability to succeed in the class.

current_lessons_end.text: You decided to focus on the current lessons while using the extra sessions to fill gaps as they appeared. This approach kept you up to date with the class while slowly addressing your knowledge gaps. It was challenging because you had to juggle new and old material at the same time. However, the teacher's support made it possible. You managed to pass the course, though you felt that you could have benefited from a stronger foundation. You made a mental note to review the basics during the next break.

test_prep_end.text: Your study group focused on preparing for upcoming tests. You practiced with sample questions and timed yourselves. local_program_end.text: You applied for the local program and were accepted. The program turned out to be excellent and exceeded your expectations. You learned a great deal and made valuable connections in your field. You realized that you did not need to travel far to find meaningful opportunities. The delay had actually worked in your favor. You learned that patience can sometimes lead to better outcomes than rushing into a decision.

future_help_end.text: You asked your friend if they would help you attend a similar event in the future. Your friend immediately agreed and said they would even contribute to the ticket. You felt relieved that your sacrifice was appreciated and reciprocated. A few months later, another event was announced and you both registered together. This time, nothing got in the way and you had an amazing time side by side. Your friendship grew stronger because of the way you handled the situation.

start.question: Do you attend the event as planned or cancel to help your friend move?
start.text: You have been saving money for months to attend The Business Trip. You worked part-time jobs and reduced your expenses to make it possible. Finally, you have enough money and the event is next week. But now your friend has asked you to help them move to a new apartment on the same day. They really need your help and you feel torn between your plans and your friendship. You promised yourself you would attend this event, but you also do not want to let your friend down.

attend_event.question: Do you try to help your friend before the event or send them a gift afterward?
attend_event.text: You decided to attend the event as planned. You explained to your friend that you had been saving for months and could not miss it. Your friend was understanding but you could hear the disappointment in their voice. You felt guilty but also knew that you had worked hard for this opportunity. On the day of the event, you tried to enjoy yourself but your friend kept crossing your mind. You wondered if you had made the right choice.

help_before_end.text: You woke up early on the day of the event and went straight to your friend's apartment. You helped them pack boxes and load furniture for three hours. Your friend was surprised and touched that you came. After finishing the heavy work, you apologized again and left for the event. You arrived a bit late but you still managed to enjoy most of it. You felt good because you had helped your friend and still made it to the event. It was the best of both worlds.

let_go_end.text: You decided not to ask for anything in return. Helping your friend was its own reward and you did not want to keep score. Although you missed the event, you felt content knowing you had been there for someone who mattered to you. Sometimes being a good friend is more important than any event.

help_friend.text: You decided to help your friend move. It was not an easy decision because you had been looking forward to The Business Trip for months. You both agreed to plan something fun together next weekend. The experience taught you that honest communication can preserve friendships even when plans conflict.

start.text: You have been working on a personal project about A Charity Event for several weeks. You are passionate about it and you have put a lot of effort into making it perfect. more_feedback_end.text: After revising your work, you asked for feedback from several people whose opinions you respected. Some of them gave you additional suggestions while others said the revision was a significant improvement. You incorporated the best suggestions and your project became stronger with each iteration. By the time you completed the final version, it was far better than your original concept. You learned that good work is not born perfect but is refined through continuous improvement and an open mind.

trust_judgment_end.text: You decided to trust your own judgment after the revision. You had carefully considered the feedback and made the changes you thought were necessary. Now it was time to stand by your decisions. You submitted the final version with confidence. The response was generally positive and you felt validated in your choices. The experience taught you to balance external input with your own instincts.

trust_vision.text: You decided to trust your original vision. You believed in the ideas behind your project and felt that the criticism came from a different perspective that did not fully understand your goals. You made a few minor adjustments but kept the core of your work intact. When you presented the final version, some people appreciated your boldness while others still saw issues. You felt satisfied that you had stayed true to yourself, even if not everyone agreed with your choices.

explain_choices_end.text: You wrote a detailed explanation of your creative choices and shared it alongside your project. You described the thinking process behind each major decision and why you believed it was the right approach. Some people changed their minds after reading your explanation. Others still disagreed but respected your thoughtfulness. Either way, you felt that you had communicated your vision clearly and that was what mattered most to you.

You continued the study group for the rest of the course and it became one of the most valuable parts of your learning experience.

Your family says they support whatever decision you make, but you can tell they will miss you. You need to decide whether this opportunity is worth the temporary sacrifice.

explore_city_end.text: You decided to balance work with exploring the city. On weekdays, you focused on your responsibilities. On weekends, you visited museums, tried local restaurants, and walked through different neighborhoods. You discovered that the city had a rich history and vibrant culture. The experiences outside of work enriched your overall journey and gave you a broader perspective. When you returned home, you had not only professional growth but also wonderful memories and new friends.

stay_home.question: Do you apply for the local program or wait for a better opportunity?
stay_home.text: You decided to stay home. The opportunity was tempting but you felt that you were not ready to leave everything behind. You continued with your usual routine and tried not to think about what you might be missing. However, you could not help wondering if you had made a mistake. You started looking for local opportunities that could offer similar growth without requiring you to move. A few weeks later, you found a promising local program that excited you just as much.

focus_work_end.text: You decided to focus entirely on your work. You arrived early every day and stayed late whenever necessary. Your dedication impressed your supervisors and you made excellent progress on the projects assigned to you. By the end of the two months, you had achieved more than you had hoped. Your supervisors offered you a letter of recommendation and expressed interest in working with you again. You returned home with a great sense of accomplishment and new skills that would benefit your career.

take_opportunity.text: You decided to take the opportunity. You packed your bags and said goodbye to your family at the airport. But as the days passed, you started to adapt to your new environment. You met interesting people, learned new skills, and discovered things about yourself that you had never known before.

local_program_end.text: You applied for the local program and were accepted. The program turned out to be excellent and exceeded your expectations. You learned a great deal and made valuable connections in your field. You realized that you did not need to travel far to find meaningful opportunities. Being close to your support system actually helped you take more risks and grow more confidently. You felt grateful that things worked out the way they did.

wait_better_end.text: You decided to wait for a better opportunity. You continued your daily life and kept an eye out for something that would be a perfect fit. The waiting period gave you time to prepare and improve your skills. After a few months, an even better opportunity came along, this time closer to home. You applied and succeeded. The delay had actually worked in your favor. You learned that patience can sometimes lead to better outcomes than rushing into a decision.

decline_politely.question: Do you look for a similar opportunity that fits your schedule better, or focus on your current projects?
decline_politely.text: You decided to decline the invitation. You wrote a polite email explaining that you could not participate due to other commitments. It was not an easy decision because the opportunity was genuinely interesting. However, you knew your limits and did not want to take on more than you could handle. After sending the email, you felt a mixture of relief and regret. You wondered if you had made the right choice.

start.question: Do you accept the invitation and prepare thoroughly, or decline politely to avoid the pressure?

It sounds like a wonderful opportunity, but it would also require a lot of time and effort. Part of you is excited about the possibility, while another part feels nervous about the commitment. You discussed it with your family and they said you should make your own decision. Now you are sitting in your room, weighing the pros and cons carefully.

current_projects_end.text: You decided to focus your energy on your current projects instead. You had several things on your plate already and they deserved your full attention. You created a plan to complete each project step by step. Without the distraction of a new commitment, you made excellent progress on everything you were working on. By the end of the month, you had finished two projects and started a third. You felt productive and satisfied with what you had accomplished.

another_opp_end.text: You started looking for another opportunity that would fit better with your schedule. You searched online and asked friends if they knew of any similar events. Within a week, you found a smaller, less demanding version of The Networking Event that seemed perfect for you. You applied and were accepted. The experience was rewarding and you met some wonderful people. You realized that sometimes declining one door allows another, more suitable door to open. You did not regret your decision at all.

strengths_end.text: You decided to focus on strengthening your existing skills. You already had a solid foundation, so you worked on refining your technique and adding new dimensions to your abilities. Your confidence grew as you saw yourself becoming even better at the things you already enjoyed. During the event, your strengths shone through and impressed many people. You received positive feedback and felt validated in your approach. However, you also noticed that ignoring your weaknesses completely might cause problems in the long run.

accept_prepare.question: Do you focus on improving your weaknesses or strengthening your existing skills?
accept_prepare.text: You decided to accept the invitation. You replied to the email confirming your participation and felt a rush of excitement mixed with nervousness. Your friends noticed your dedication and offered to help you practice. You felt supported and motivated to do your best.

weaknesses_end.text: You decided to focus on improving your weaknesses. It was not always comfortable because it meant doing things you were not naturally good at. You practiced every day and asked for feedback from people who had more experience. Slowly but surely, you started to notice improvements. By the time the event arrived, you felt much more confident than you had at the beginning. The hard work paid off and you performed better than you expected. You learned that facing your weaknesses directly is the best way to overcome them.

speak_itself_end.text: You decided to let the work speak for itself without additional commentary. You believed that good work does not need explanations. Some viewers understood your vision immediately while others struggled to connect with it. You accepted both reactions gracefully. The experience reinforced your belief that art and creativity are subjective. You were proud of what you had created and that was enough.

start.question: Do you accept the criticism and revise your work, or trust your original vision?
start.text: You have been working on a personal project about A Film Review for several weeks. You are passionate about it and you have put a lot of effort into making it perfect. Part of you wants to defend your work, but another part recognizes that the criticism might be valid. You are standing at a crossroads, wondering how to move forward.

more_feedback_end.text: After revising your work, you asked for feedback from several people whose opinions you respected. Some of them gave you additional suggestions while others said the revision was a significant improvement. You incorporated the best suggestions and your project became stronger with each iteration. By the time you completed the final version, it was far better than your original concept. You learned that good work is not born perfect but is refined through continuous improvement and an open mind.

trust_judgment_end.text: You decided to trust your own judgment after the revision. You had carefully considered the feedback and made the changes you thought were necessary. Now it was time to stand by your decisions. You submitted the final version with confidence. The response was generally positive and you felt validated in your choices. The experience taught you to balance external input with your own instincts.

trust_vision.question: Do you explain your creative choices publicly or let the work speak for itself?
trust_vision.text: You decided to trust your original vision. You believed in the ideas behind your project and felt that the criticism came from a different perspective that did not fully understand your goals. You made a few minor adjustments but kept the core of your work intact. When you presented the final version, some people appreciated your boldness while others still saw issues. You felt satisfied that you had stayed true to yourself, even if not everyone agreed with your choices.

explain_choices_end.text: You wrote a detailed explanation of your creative choices and shared it alongside your project. You described the thinking process behind each major decision and why you believed it was the right approach. Some people changed their minds after reading your explanation. Others still disagreed but respected your thoughtfulness. Either way, you felt that you had communicated your vision clearly and that was what mattered most to you.

revise.text: You decided to accept the criticism and revise your work. It was not easy to hear that your project had flaws, but you reminded yourself that feedback helps you grow. You sat down with a notebook and listed all the points that needed improvement. Then you started making changes one by one, testing each modification carefully. The process took longer than you expected, but gradually the project began to transform. You started to see that the criticism had actually helped you make your work better.

start.question: Do you ask the teacher for extra help or form a study group with classmates?

But now the material is getting more difficult and you are struggling to keep up. The teacher moves quickly and you feel like you are falling behind. Some of your classmates seem to understand everything easily, which makes you feel even more frustrated. You are considering whether you should continue or drop the class.

review_end.text: Your study group focused on reviewing past lessons. Each member took turns explaining a topic they understood well. This helped everyone see things from different perspectives. Slowly, the material that had seemed impossible started to become clear. You realized that teaching others was also a great way to reinforce your own understanding. After a few weeks, everyone in the group had improved significantly.

Five people replied and agreed to meet twice a week. The first session was a bit awkward but everyone contributed something useful. You discovered that some of your classmates were struggling with the same concepts as you. Working together made the difficult material feel more manageable.

fundamentals_end.text: You decided to go back to the fundamentals. With the teacher's guidance, you reviewed the basic concepts that everything else was built upon. It felt a bit like starting over, but you soon realized that your foundation had been weaker than you thought. Once you strengthened it, the advanced material started to make much more sense. Your confidence grew steadily and you began to enjoy the class again. By the end of the course, you achieved a grade that you were truly proud of.

The teacher listened patiently and smiled reassuringly. They offered to meet with you during their office hours twice a week. They also gave you some additional resources that might help you understand the concepts better. You left the conversation feeling much more optimistic about your ability to succeed in the class.

current_lessons_end.text: You decided to focus on the current lessons while using the extra sessions to fill gaps as they appeared. This approach kept you up to date with the class while slowly addressing your knowledge gaps. It was challenging because you had to juggle new and old material at the same time. However, the teacher's support made it possible. You managed to pass the course, though you felt that you could have benefited from a stronger foundation. You made a mental note to review the basics during the next break.

start.question: Do you attend the event as planned or cancel to help your friend move?
start.text: You have been saving money for months to attend The Science Fair. You worked part-time jobs and reduced your expenses to make it possible. Finally, you have enough money and the event is next week. But now your friend has asked you to help them move to a new apartment on the same day. They really need your help and you feel torn between your plans and your friendship. You promised yourself you would attend this event, but you also do not want to let your friend down.

attend_event.question: Do you try to help your friend before the event or send them a gift afterward?
attend_event.text: You decided to attend the event as planned. You explained to your friend that you had been saving for months and could not miss it. Your friend was understanding but you could hear the disappointment in their voice. You felt guilty but also knew that you had worked hard for this opportunity. On the day of the event, you tried to enjoy yourself but your friend kept crossing your mind. You wondered if you had made the right choice.

help_before_end.text: You woke up early on the day of the event and went straight to your friend's apartment. You helped them pack boxes and load furniture for three hours. Your friend was surprised and touched that you came. After finishing the heavy work, you apologized again and left for the event. You arrived a bit late but you still managed to enjoy most of it. You felt good because you had helped your friend and still made it to the event. It was the best of both worlds.

let_go_end.text: You decided not to ask for anything in return. Helping your friend was its own reward and you did not want to keep score. Your friend noticed your generosity and respected you even more for it. You helped them unpack and organize their new apartment. By the end of the day, you had made their new place feel like home. Although you missed the event, you felt content knowing you had been there for someone who mattered to you. Sometimes being a good friend is more important than any event.

help_friend.text: You decided to help your friend move. It was not an easy decision because you had been looking forward to The Science Fair for months. They said it was possible, which was a relief. Your friend was extremely grateful and promised to make it up to you.

It sounds like a wonderful opportunity, but it would also require a lot of time and effort. Part of you is excited about the possibility, while another part feels nervous about the commitment. You discussed it with your family and they said you should make your own decision. Now you are sitting in your room, weighing the pros and cons carefully.

current_projects_end.text: You decided to focus your energy on your current projects instead. You had several things on your plate already and they deserved your full attention. You created a plan to complete each project step by step. Without the distraction of a new commitment, you made excellent progress on everything you were working on. By the end of the month, you had finished two projects and started a third. You felt productive and satisfied with what you had accomplished.

another_opp_end.text: You started looking for another opportunity that would fit better with your schedule. You searched online and asked friends if they knew of any similar events. Within a week, you found a smaller, less demanding version of A Travel Blog that seemed perfect for you. You applied and were accepted. The experience was rewarding and you met some wonderful people. You realized that sometimes declining one door allows another, more suitable door to open. You did not regret your decision at all.

strengths_end.text: You decided to focus on strengthening your existing skills. You already had a solid foundation, so you worked on refining your technique and adding new dimensions to your abilities. Your confidence grew as you saw yourself becoming even better at the things you already enjoyed. During the event, your strengths shone through and impressed many people. You received positive feedback and felt validated in your approach. However, you also noticed that ignoring your weaknesses completely might cause problems in the long run.

accept_prepare.question: Do you focus on improving your weaknesses or strengthening your existing skills?
accept_prepare.text: You decided to accept the invitation. You replied to the email confirming your participation and felt a rush of excitement mixed with nervousness. Over the next few days, you started preparing by gathering information and practicing relevant skills. You created a schedule to make sure you would have enough time to get ready. Your friends noticed your dedication and offered to help you practice. You felt supported and motivated to do your best.

weaknesses_end.text: You decided to focus on improving your weaknesses. It was not always comfortable because it meant doing things you were not naturally good at. You practiced every day and asked for feedback from people who had more experience. Slowly but surely, you started to notice improvements. By the time the event arrived, you felt much more confident than you had at the beginning. The hard work paid off and you performed better than you expected. You learned that facing your weaknesses directly is the best way to overcome them.

start.question: Do you take the opportunity and gain the experience, or stay home and maintain your current routine?
start.text: You have been offered a short-term opportunity related to The Cooking Blog in another city. It would be a valuable experience for your personal and professional growth. However, it would mean leaving your family and friends for two months. You have never been away from home for that long before. Your family says they support whatever decision you make, but you can tell they will miss you. You need to decide whether this opportunity is worth the temporary sacrifice.

explore_city_end.text: You decided to balance work with exploring the city. On weekdays, you focused on your responsibilities. On weekends, you visited museums, tried local restaurants, and walked through different neighborhoods. You discovered that the city had a rich history and vibrant culture. The experiences outside of work enriched your overall journey and gave you a broader perspective. When you returned home, you had not only professional growth but also wonderful memories and new friends.

stay_home.question: Do you apply for the local program or wait for a better opportunity?
stay_home.text: You decided to stay home. The opportunity was tempting but you felt that you were not ready to leave everything behind. You continued with your usual routine and tried not to think about what you might be missing. However, you could not help wondering if you had made a mistake. You started looking for local opportunities that could offer similar growth without requiring you to move. A few weeks later, you found a promising local program that excited you just as much.

focus_work_end.text: You decided to focus entirely on your work. You arrived early every day and stayed late whenever necessary. Your dedication impressed your supervisors and you made excellent progress on the projects assigned to you. By the end of the two months, you had achieved more than you had hoped. Your supervisors offered you a letter of recommendation and expressed interest in working with you again. You returned home with a great sense of accomplishment and new skills that would benefit your career.

take_opportunity.question: Do you focus entirely on work or also explore the city during your free time?
take_opportunity.text: You decided to take the opportunity. You packed your bags and said goodbye to your family at the airport. The first week was difficult because everything was unfamiliar and you missed home terribly. You called your parents every evening and that helped a little. But as the days passed, you started to adapt to your new environment. You met interesting people, learned new skills, and discovered things about yourself that you had never known before.

local_program_end.text: You applied for the local program and were accepted. The program turned out to be excellent and exceeded your expectations. You learned a great deal and made valuable connections in your field. You realized that you did not need to travel far to find meaningful opportunities. Being close to your support system actually helped you take more risks and grow more confidently. You felt grateful that things worked out the way they did.

wait_better_end.text: You decided to wait for a better opportunity. You continued your daily life and kept an eye out for something that would be a perfect fit. The waiting period gave you time to prepare and improve your skills. After a few months, an even better opportunity came along, this time closer to home. You applied and succeeded. The delay had actually worked in your favor. You learned that patience can sometimes lead to better outcomes than rushing into a decision.

decline_politely.text: You decided to decline the invitation. You wrote a polite email explaining that you could not participate due to other commitments. After sending the email, you felt a mixture of relief and regret. You wondered if you had made the right choice.

start.question: Do you attend the event as planned or cancel to help your friend move?
start.text: You have been saving money for months to attend A Cooking Show. You worked part-time jobs and reduced your expenses to make it possible. Finally, you have enough money and the event is next week. But now your friend has asked you to help them move to a new apartment on the same day. They really need your help and you feel torn between your plans and your friendship. You promised yourself you would attend this event, but you also do not want to let your friend down.

attend_event.question: Do you try to help your friend before the event or send them a gift afterward?
attend_event.text: You decided to attend the event as planned. You explained to your friend that you had been saving for months and could not miss it. Your friend was understanding but you could hear the disappointment in their voice. You felt guilty but also knew that you had worked hard for this opportunity. On the day of the event, you tried to enjoy yourself but your friend kept crossing your mind. You wondered if you had made the right choice.

help_before_end.text: You woke up early on the day of the event and went straight to your friend's apartment. You helped them pack boxes and load furniture for three hours. Your friend was surprised and touched that you came. After finishing the heavy work, you apologized again and left for the event. You arrived a bit late but you still managed to enjoy most of it. You felt good because you had helped your friend and still made it to the event. It was the best of both worlds.

let_go_end.text: You decided not to ask for anything in return. Helping your friend was its own reward and you did not want to keep score. Your friend noticed your generosity and respected you even more for it. You helped them unpack and organize their new apartment. By the end of the day, you had made their new place feel like home. Although you missed the event, you felt content knowing you had been there for someone who mattered to you. Sometimes being a good friend is more important than any event.

help_friend.question: Do you ask your friend to help you attend a future event or just let it go?
help_friend.text: You decided to help your friend move. It was not an easy decision because you had been looking forward to A Cooking Show for months. But friendship was important to you and you knew your friend needed you. You called the event organizers to explain the situation and asked if you could transfer your ticket to someone else. They said it was possible, which was a relief. Your friend was extremely grateful and promised to make it up to you.

gift_later_end.text: After the event, you bought your friend a nice housewarming gift. You chose a beautiful plant and a card where you wrote a heartfelt apology. When you gave it to them, your friend smiled and said they understood. They told you that you were a good friend and that the gift was lovely. You both agreed to plan something fun together next weekend. The experience taught you that honest communication can preserve friendships even when plans conflict.

start.question: Do you ask the teacher for extra help or form a study group with classmates?
start.text: You recently started a new class related to The Sports Event. At first, everything seemed interesting and you were excited to learn. But now the material is getting more difficult and you are struggling to keep up. The teacher moves quickly and you feel like you are falling behind. Some of your classmates seem to understand everything easily, which makes you feel even more frustrated. You are considering whether you should continue or drop the class.

review_end.text: Your study group focused on reviewing past lessons. Each member took turns explaining a topic they understood well. This helped everyone see things from different perspectives. Slowly, the material that had seemed impossible started to become clear. You realized that teaching others was also a great way to reinforce your own understanding. After a few weeks, everyone in the group had improved significantly.

study_group.question: Do you focus on reviewing past lessons or preparing for upcoming tests?
study_group.text: You decided to form a study group with some of your classmates. You posted a message in the class group chat asking who would be interested. Five people replied and agreed to meet twice a week. The first session was a bit awkward but everyone contributed something useful. You discovered that some of your classmates were struggling with the same concepts as you. Working together made the difficult material feel more manageable.

fundamentals_end.text: You decided to go back to the fundamentals. With the teacher's guidance, you reviewed the basic concepts that everything else was built upon. It felt a bit like starting over, but you soon realized that your foundation had been weaker than you thought. Once you strengthened it, the advanced material started to make much more sense. Your confidence grew steadily and you began to enjoy the class again. By the end of the course, you achieved a grade that you were truly proud of.

teacher_help.question: Do you focus on the fundamentals first or jump ahead to the current lessons?
teacher_help.text: You gathered your courage and approached the teacher after class. You explained that you were having difficulty keeping up with the material. The teacher listened patiently and smiled reassuringly. They offered to meet with you during their office hours twice a week. They also gave you some additional resources that might help you understand the concepts better. You left the conversation feeling much more optimistic about your ability to succeed in the class.

current_lessons_end.text: You decided to focus on the current lessons while using the extra sessions to fill gaps as they appeared. This approach kept you up to date with the class while slowly addressing your knowledge gaps. It was challenging because you had to juggle new and old material at the same time. However, the teacher's support made it possible. You managed to pass the course, though you felt that you could have benefited from a stronger foundation. You made a mental note to review the basics during the next break.

test_prep_end.text: Your study group focused on preparing for upcoming tests. You practiced with sample questions and timed yourselves. It was intense but effective because you could immediately apply what you were learning. When the test day arrived, you felt prepared and confident. The results were better than you had expected. You continued the study group for the rest of the course and it became one of the most valuable parts of your learning experience.

start.question: Do you accept the criticism and revise your work, or trust your original vision?
start.text: You have been working on a personal project about The Music Practice for several weeks. You are passionate about it and you have put a lot of effort into making it perfect. Part of you wants to defend your work, but another part recognizes that the criticism might be valid. You are standing at a crossroads, wondering how to move forward.

more_feedback_end.text: After revising your work, you asked for feedback from several people whose opinions you respected. Some of them gave you additional suggestions while others said the revision was a significant improvement. You incorporated the best suggestions and your project became stronger with each iteration. By the time you completed the final version, it was far better than your original concept. You learned that good work is not born perfect but is refined through continuous improvement and an open mind.

trust_judgment_end.text: You decided to trust your own judgment after the revision. You had carefully considered the feedback and made the changes you thought were necessary. The experience taught you to balance external input with your own instincts.

You believed in the ideas behind your project and felt that the criticism came from a different perspective that did not fully understand your goals. The experience reinforced your belief that art and creativity are subjective. You were proud of what you had created and that was enough.

start.question: Do you accept the criticism and revise your work, or trust your original vision?
start.text: You have been working on a personal project about The Healthy Habit for several weeks. You are passionate about it and you have put a lot of effort into making it perfect. However, you recently received some feedback that was quite critical. The person who reviewed your work pointed out several problems you had not noticed. Part of you wants to defend your work, but another part recognizes that the criticism might be valid. You are standing at a crossroads, wondering how to move forward.

more_feedback_end.text: After revising your work, you asked for feedback from several people whose opinions you respected. Some of them gave you additional suggestions while others said the revision was a significant improvement. You incorporated the best suggestions and your project became stronger with each iteration. By the time you completed the final version, it was far better than your original concept. You learned that good work is not born perfect but is refined through continuous improvement and an open mind.

trust_judgment_end.text: You decided to trust your own judgment after the revision. You had carefully considered the feedback and made the changes you thought were necessary. Now it was time to stand by your decisions. You submitted the final version with confidence. The response was generally positive and you felt validated in your choices. The experience taught you to balance external input with your own instincts.

trust_vision.question: Do you explain your creative choices publicly or let the work speak for itself?
trust_vision.text: You decided to trust your original vision. You believed in the ideas behind your project and felt that the criticism came from a different perspective that did not fully understand your goals. You made a few minor adjustments but kept the core of your work intact. When you presented the final version, some people appreciated your boldness while others still saw issues. You felt satisfied that you had stayed true to yourself, even if not everyone agreed with your choices.

explain_choices_end.text: You wrote a detailed explanation of your creative choices and shared it alongside your project. You described the thinking process behind each major decision and why you believed it was the right approach. Some people changed their minds after reading your explanation. Others still disagreed but respected your thoughtfulness. Either way, you felt that you had communicated your vision clearly and that was what mattered most to you.

revise.question: Do you ask for more feedback after revising or trust your own judgment?
revise.text: You decided to accept the criticism and revise your work. It was not easy to hear that your project had flaws, but you reminded yourself that feedback helps you grow. You sat down with a notebook and listed all the points that needed improvement. Then you started making changes one by one, testing each modification carefully. The process took longer than you expected, but gradually the project began to transform. You started to see that the criticism had actually helped you make your work better.

future_help_end.text: You asked your friend if they would help you attend a similar event in the future. Your friend immediately agreed and said they would even contribute to the ticket. You felt relieved that your sacrifice was appreciated and reciprocated. A few months later, another event was announced and you both registered together. This time, nothing got in the way and you had an amazing time side by side. Your friendship grew stronger because of the way you handled the situation.

start.question: Do you attend the event as planned or cancel to help your friend move?
start.text: You have been saving money for months to attend A Dance Show. You worked part-time jobs and reduced your expenses to make it possible. Finally, you have enough money and the event is next week. But now your friend has asked you to help them move to a new apartment on the same day. They really need your help and you feel torn between your plans and your friendship. You promised yourself you would attend this event, but you also do not want to let your friend down.

attend_event.question: Do you try to help your friend before the event or send them a gift afterward?
attend_event.text: You decided to attend the event as planned. You explained to your friend that you had been saving for months and could not miss it. Your friend was understanding but you could hear the disappointment in their voice. You felt guilty but also knew that you had worked hard for this opportunity. On the day of the event, you tried to enjoy yourself but your friend kept crossing your mind. You wondered if you had made the right choice.

help_before_end.text: You woke up early on the day of the event and went straight to your friend's apartment. You helped them pack boxes and load furniture for three hours. Your friend was surprised and touched that you came. After finishing the heavy work, you apologized again and left for the event. You arrived a bit late but you still managed to enjoy most of it. You felt good because you had helped your friend and still made it to the event. It was the best of both worlds.

let_go_end.text: You decided not to ask for anything in return. Helping your friend was its own reward and you did not want to keep score. Your friend noticed your generosity and respected you even more for it. You helped them unpack and organize their new apartment. By the end of the day, you had made their new place feel like home. Although you missed the event, you felt content knowing you had been there for someone who mattered to you. Sometimes being a good friend is more important than any event.

help_friend.question: Do you ask your friend to help you attend a future event or just let it go?
help_friend.text: You decided to help your friend move. It was not an easy decision because you had been looking forward to A Dance Show for months. But friendship was important to you and you knew your friend needed you. You called the event organizers to explain the situation and asked if you could transfer your ticket to someone else. They said it was possible, which was a relief. Your friend was extremely grateful and promised to make it up to you.

gift_later_end.text: After the event, you bought your friend a nice housewarming gift. You chose a beautiful plant and a card where you wrote a heartfelt apology. When you gave it to them, your friend smiled and said they understood. They told you that you were a good friend and that the gift was lovely. You both agreed to plan something fun together next weekend. The experience taught you that honest communication can preserve friendships even when plans conflict.

start.question: Do you take the opportunity and gain the experience, or stay home and maintain your current routine?
start.text: You have been offered a short-term opportunity related to The Writing Workshop in another city. It would be a valuable experience for your personal and professional growth. However, it would mean leaving your family and friends for two months. You have never been away from home for that long before. Your family says they support whatever decision you make, but you can tell they will miss you. You need to decide whether this opportunity is worth the temporary sacrifice.

explore_city_end.text: You decided to balance work with exploring the city. On weekdays, you focused on your responsibilities. On weekends, you visited museums, tried local restaurants, and walked through different neighborhoods. You discovered that the city had a rich history and vibrant culture. The experiences outside of work enriched your overall journey and gave you a broader perspective. When you returned home, you had not only professional growth but also wonderful memories and new friends.

stay_home.question: Do you apply for the local program or wait for a better opportunity?
stay_home.text: You decided to stay home. The opportunity was tempting but you felt that you were not ready to leave everything behind. You continued with your usual routine and tried not to think about what you might be missing. However, you could not help wondering if you had made a mistake. You started looking for local opportunities that could offer similar growth without requiring you to move. A few weeks later, you found a promising local program that excited you just as much.

focus_work_end.text: You decided to focus entirely on your work. You arrived early every day and stayed late whenever necessary. Your dedication impressed your supervisors and you made excellent progress on the projects assigned to you. By the end of the two months, you had achieved more than you had hoped. Your supervisors offered you a letter of recommendation and expressed interest in working with you again. You returned home with a great sense of accomplishment and new skills that would benefit your career.

take_opportunity.question: Do you focus entirely on work or also explore the city during your free time?
take_opportunity.text: You decided to take the opportunity. You packed your bags and said goodbye to your family at the airport. The first week was difficult because everything was unfamiliar and you missed home terribly. You called your parents every evening and that helped a little. But as the days passed, you started to adapt to your new environment. You met interesting people, learned new skills, and discovered things about yourself that you had never known before.

local_program_end.text: You applied for the local program and were accepted. The program turned out to be excellent and exceeded your expectations. You learned a great deal and made valuable connections in your field. You realized that you did not need to travel far to find meaningful opportunities. Being close to your support system actually helped you take more risks and grow more confidently. You felt grateful that things worked out the way they did.

wait_better_end.text: You decided to wait for a better opportunity. You continued your daily life and kept an eye out for something that would be a perfect fit. The waiting period gave you time to prepare and improve your skills. After a few months, an even better opportunity came along, this time closer to home. You applied and succeeded. The delay had actually worked in your favor. You learned that patience can sometimes lead to better outcomes than rushing into a decision.
